quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue $216 million, up 3% year-over-year and sequentially, above the high end of guidance as delayed semiconductor design releases from fiscal Q2 recovered. IC revenue $155 million (72% of total), up nearly 5% YoY and sequentially, with the high-end portion a record 44% of IC revenue; mainstream declined to $86 million on node migration; FPD revenue $61 million near all-time highs.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $216 million (+3%); IC $155 million; high-end 44% of IC (record); FPD $61 million

quarterly_data.signal: Gross margin 33%, improved sequentially on mix and operating leverage; operating margin 21%; GAAP diluted EPS $0.49, non-GAAP $0.50; operating cash flow $76 million (35% of revenue); total cash and short-term investments $673 million including $504 million held within joint ventures (50.01% ownership).
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 33%; operating margin 21%; EPS $0.49 GAAP / $0.50 non-GAAP; cash $673 million

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q4 guidance widened: revenue $207 million-$227 million, operating margin 19%-24%, non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.40-$0.56. Visibility into design-release timing is more uncertain because of high fab utilization rates, high memory costs and geopolitical conditions; one high-end mask set can swing a couple million plus dollars in a quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $207 million-$227 million; operating margin 19%-24%; EPS $0.40-$0.56

quarterly_data.signal: With wafer utilization high, fabs are prioritizing higher-profitability projects and expanding capacity at higher technology nodes; node migration actions especially at 28 nm, 22 nm and 14 nm are occurring across a broad set of customers and geographies, benefiting the high-end IC business since node migration to high-end mask sets carries higher ASPs per chip design.

Korea expansion to 8 nm: clean room preparation substantially completed, initial tools received, planned installations on schedule; more advanced 8 nm capabilities to be delivered in Korea over the next year and a half, positioning Photronics to capture increased outsourcing from captive mask shops.
quarterly_data.figure: 8 nm capability in Korea over the next year and a half

quarterly_data.signal: Allen, Texas facility: targeting initial revenue late this fiscal quarter, with the geographic diversification contribution reflected in fiscal 2027 revenue and beyond; Allen adds capacity in the higher end of mainstream (mid-range nodes such as 65 nm) and frees Boise to focus on the high end; mainstream in the U.S. expected to increase in fiscal 2027 as Allen captures share at higher-end nodes.

EUV strategy: for several years Photronics has leveraged partnerships with industry leaders to supply EUV R&D masks and solutions to customers while the full turnkey EUV merchant market develops, and has also supplied EUV-related masks to the semiconductor equipment supply chain; it will gradually introduce internal EUV capabilities and make the significant turnkey capex only once the merchant market makes the internal rate of return viable.

Fiscal 2026 capex guidance updated to $255 million-$305 million from $330 million; fiscal year-to-date capex $130 million (Q3 $37 million). The projects and timelines are unchanged, but the cadence of orders and vendor delivery of high-value tools shifts spending, and any spend that slips carries into fiscal 2027, so the end-of-life tool upgrade peak may be in 2027 rather than 2026. Liquidity may be supplemented by borrowing to fund the EUV investment strategy.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 capex $255 million-$305 million (prior $330 million); YTD $130 million
